merger_name: AUB – further interest in Sura Technology
merger_description:
Austagencies Pty Ltd (**Austagencies**), a wholly owned subsidiary of AUB Group Limited (**AUB**), proposes to acquire an additional 20% of the issued share capital in Sura Technology Risks Pty Ltd (**Sura Technology**) by way of a purchase of shares from an existing minority shareholder, D J & S Underwood Pty Ltd as trustee for the D J & S Underwood Family Trust (the **Acquisition**). On completion, Austagencies will hold 70% of the issued share capital in Sura Technology, with the balance retained by two other minority shareholders.

Austagencies is a collection of Australian underwriting agencies providing underwriting services for general insurance products (primarily under the 360 Underwriting Solutions brand), specialty insurance products designed for specific industries (under the SURA brands), and strata insurance (under the Longitude, Rubix and Strata Unit Underwriters brands).

AUB Group Limited (ASX: AUB) is an ASX200 global insurance broking group with a diversified portfolio spanning General and Specialist Retail Brokers, Authorised Representative and Broking Networks, Managing General Agents and Underwriting Agencies, Wholesale Brokers, InsurTech platforms, and specialist Claims and Loss Adjustment services. AUB operates from approximately 580 locations, with ~6,000 people supporting around 1.2 million clients and placing more than AUD$11 billion in premiums with local and international insurers each year.

Sura Technology is an Australian underwriting agency which provides underwriting services for specialty insurance products designed for technology businesses. Sura Technology’s primary activities relate to providing a technology package which includes cyber cover for first and third party risks for technology providers, professional indemnity for technology risks and public and products liability for technology businesses. Sura Technology also provides underwriting services for a standalone cyber insurance policy.

determination_table_content.details:
AUB Group Limited (AUB), together with its wholly owned subsidiary
Austagencies Pty Ltd (Austagencies), applied for a notification
waiver in respect of Austagencies’ proposed acquisition of an
additional 20% of the issued share capital in Sura Technology Risks
Pty Ltd (Sura Technology) by way of a purchase of shares from an
existing minority shareholder, D J & S Underwood Pty Ltd as trustee
for the D J & S Underwood Family Trust, as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).
On completion of the Acquisition, Austagencies will hold 70% of the
issued share capital in Sura Technology, with the balance retained by
two other minority shareholders.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Austagencies, is a collection of Australian underwriting
agencies providing underwriting services for general insurance
products (primarily under the 360 Underwriting Solutions brand),
specialty insurance products designed for specific industries (under
the SURA brands), and strata insurance (under the Longitude, Rubix
and Strata Unit Underwriters brands).
Austagencies is a wholly owned subsidiary of AUB, which is an
ASX200 global insurance broking group with a diversified portfolio
spanning General and Specialist Retail Brokers, Authorised
Representative and Broking Networks, Managing General Agents and
Underwriting Agencies, Wholesale Brokers, InsurTech platforms, and
specialist Claims and Loss Adjustment services. AUB operates from
approximately 580 locations, with ~6,000 people supporting around
1.2 million clients and placing more than AUD$11 billion in premiums
with local and international insurers each year.
The target, Sura Technology, is an Australian underwriting agency
which provides underwriting services for specialty insurance
products designed for technology businesses. Sura Technology’s
primary activities relate to providing a technology package which
includes cyber cover for first and third party risks for technology
providers, professional indemnity for technology risks and public and
products liability for technology businesses. Sura Technology also
provides underwriting services for a standalone cyber insurance
policy.
Austagencies and Sura Technology both supply insurance
underwriting services in Australia.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition as it is unlikely to result in any substantive
change in the control of Sura Technology.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
